title: One Open Patient Payment Plan per Patient
content:
**Patient Financial Services policy, Patient Payment Plan: number of plans a patient may hold**

1. A patient may hold at most 1 Patient Payment Plan at a time.
2. A new payment plan is not set up while the patient holds one in pending signature, active or past due status; new eligible charges are added to that plan instead where its tier allows add-ons.
3. A defaulted plan blocks a new plan until its reinstatement window has passed.
4. Whether the patient already holds a plan, and in which status, is established from the payment plan records held under that patient as guarantor, as they stand before a new plan is set up; it is not taken from the patient's own account of their plans.

## The rule by status of the plan already held

| Status of the patient's existing Patient Payment Plan | May a new plan be set up? |
|---|---|
| Pending signature | No |
| Active | No |
| Past due | No |
| Defaulted | No, until that plan's reinstatement window has passed |

The limit is a count of 1 per patient, read from the records under that patient; the clause concerns the patient (guarantor), whichever plan of care the new charges come from.

## Illustrations (hypothetical)

- A patient's records show an active Patient Payment Plan on a tier that allows add-ons, and a new eligible charge has posted. No second plan is set up; under clause 2 the new charge is taken into the existing plan.
- A patient's records show a plan awaiting signature. A request for another plan is not set up while that plan is pending signature.
- A patient's records show a defaulted plan whose reinstatement window has not yet passed. Under clause 3 no new plan is set up while that window runs.
